mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 5% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered quarters, or the average return is not significantly below zero (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not significantly negative (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening industrial production, reducing corporate revenue prospects and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered instances, or the median return is not significantly below zero (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in HOUST and a fall in RSAFS over one month signals increased housing demand with constrained supply, which raises inflationary and interest-rate expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month AND RSAFS < previous month within the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the average return is not significantly negative (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in FEDFUNDS from above 5% to below 3% within two months signals a rapid policy easing, which lowers long-term yields and boosts risk asset valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls from >5% to <3% within two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not significantly above zero (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in PAYEMS and a fall in UNRATE indicates a situation where employment expands but the unemployment rate falls due to labor force participation declines, signaling demographic headwinds and weaker wage growth, which leads to muted S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases AND UNRATE decreases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered months, or the median return is not significantly below zero (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in CPIAUCSL above 3.5% for six consecutive months signals entrenched inflation, prompting expectations of sustained monetary tightening, which reduces equity valuations and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered periods, or the average return is not significantly below zero (p > 0.10).
